advances: The upper bound is for every real ambient mark and the normalized positive d-volume, after thickening. The intrinsic model before thickening uses D-volume. The construction excludes a factor c>1 over the sharp proposed constant and gives no counterexample at that constant.

proof:
The base-and-first-block points $(z_i,c_i)$ are affinely independent: the differences from $(z_1,c_1)=(0,0)$ for $i=2,\ldots,n+1$ give the $n$ base axes, and each other difference has a distinct standard axis in the $k$-block. The remaining vertex differences, taken within each group from its copy of $0$, give the $rD$ independent continuous block axes. This produces $n+d=r(D+1)-1$ independent directions among the vertices, so the hull is an ambient simplex. Its projection is $[0,1]^n$, whose integer points are the $z_i$. Extremality of $z_i$ forces every generator in a representation above $z_i$ to have that same base. Thus each integer fiber is exactly the stated simplex, and each is an isometric copy of $\Delta_D$. The finite disjoint union has intrinsic Hausdorff dimension $D$, and its normalized intrinsic measure is exactly the equal face mixture of w32-disjoint-simplex-face-join-depth.

The thickening adds only continuous coordinates. Consequently each actual integer fiber is the product of $\Delta_D+[-\varepsilon,\varepsilon]^D$ in its active block and translated intervals of length $2\varepsilon$ in the other $d-D$ coordinates. The positive volumes are identical. For a bounded continuous test function on a common compact set, replacing the shrinking interval coordinates by their centers changes the fiberwise integral against uniform probability by a uniformly vanishing amount. The active sets decrease to the compact simplex as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, and their volumes converge to its positive volume by continuity from above. Thus their uniform probabilities converge to the uniform simplex law. Each layer has mass $1/r$ for every $\varepsilon>0$, so the resulting finite sum converges weakly to $\nu$. For $0<\varepsilon\le1$ all these supports lie in the compact convex set $C_1$.

For the depth comparison, suppose probability measures $\mu_j\rightharpoonup\mu$ and $y_j\to y$. Through-mark halfspaces suffice since translating the threshold of a containing halfspace to the mark only shrinks it. Fix a nonzero normal $a$ and $\eta>0$. Eventually $\{w:a\cdot(w-y_j)\ge0\}$ is contained in the fixed closed set $H_\eta=\{w:a\cdot(w-y)\ge-\eta\}$. The closed-set upper bound for weak convergence gives $\limsup_j\operatorname{depth}_{\mu_j}(y_j)\le\mu(H_\eta)$. Equivalently one can bound $\mathbf1_{H_\eta}$ from above by bounded continuous functions decreasing to it using distance to $H_\eta$. Let $\eta\downarrow0$ and infimize over $a$ to obtain
$$
\limsup_j\operatorname{depth}_{\mu_j}(y_j)\le\operatorname{depth}_{\mu}(y).
$$
Continuity from above retains the entire limiting cap boundary. This also gives upper semicontinuity in the mark for a fixed law. Depth vanishes outside the convex hull of a compact support by strict separation, so the maximum for each $\nu_\varepsilon$ is attained on $C_1$. Take a sequence $\varepsilon_j\downarrow0$ realizing the limsup and a convergent subsequence of maximizers in $C_1$. The comparison bounds that limsup by $\max_y\operatorname{depth}_\nu(y)=\gamma_D/r$.

For fixed $n$, both $\gamma_D$ and $\gamma_{rD+r-n-1}$ tend to $1/e$ as $D\to\infty$, using $j\log(1+1/j)\to1$. For the specified $c>1$, choose $D$ with $\gamma_D<c\gamma_d$. The limsup inequality and the strict margin give the required bound at every sufficiently small positive $\varepsilon$.
statement:
Fix integers $n,D\ge1$, set $r=2^n$, $k=r-n-1$, and $d=k+rD$. Enumerate $z_1,\ldots,z_r\in\{0,1\}^n$ with $0,e_1,\ldots,e_n$ first. Decompose $\mathbb R^d=\mathbb R^k\times(\mathbb R^D)^r$, let $c_i=0$ for $i\le n+1$ and use the distinct standard vectors of $\mathbb R^k$ for the other $c_i$. Place the simplex $T_i$ at $z_i$ with first continuous block fixed at $c_i$, its $i$th $D$-block equal to $\Delta_D=\operatorname{conv}(0,e_1,\ldots,e_D)$ and all other blocks zero. Their lifted hull $J$ is a full-dimensional simplex, with integer fibers exactly $T_i$ and no other integer bases. Its normalized intrinsic $\mathcal H^D$ probability $\nu$ on the integer trace has unrestricted depth maximum $\gamma_D/r$.

For $\varepsilon>0$ the body $C_\varepsilon=J+(\{0\}^n\times[-\varepsilon,\varepsilon]^d)$ has exactly the same bases, with equal positive $d$-volume fibers $T_i+[-\varepsilon,\varepsilon]^d$. Its normalized mixed $d$-volume $\nu_\varepsilon$ converges weakly to $\nu$, and
$$
\limsup_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\max_{y\in\mathbb R^{n+d}}\operatorname{depth}_{\nu_\varepsilon}(y)\le\frac{\gamma_D}{r}.
$$
Here depth uses proper closed halfspaces and $\gamma_j=(j/(j+1))^j$. In particular, for each fixed $n\ge1$ and every $c>1$, some finite $D$ and all sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$ give $\max_y\operatorname{depth}_{\nu_\varepsilon}(y)<c\,2^{-n}\gamma_d$.
title: Binary join bodies rule out a uniform improvement even over all ambient marks
